fr.elements: Main Residence; Circular Driveway; Front Entry Area; Patio Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Access Drive
fr.considerations: Circular Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the structure to create open space between plantings and exterior walls.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so emergency vehicles can complete a full loop without stopping to turn around.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Thin dense vegetation at corners of the property where it may block a responder's view of the structure or side yards.
• Clear a defined path from the front entry area through to the rear of the property to give responders on foot a direct route when vehicle access to the rear is limited.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Curved Driveway; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin scattered trees around the house to create more open space between the trees and the structure.
• Break up the two tree clusters nearest to the structure by removing select trees to reduce the concentration of vegetation in those areas.
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the house so they are no longer touching or immediately adjacent to the walls.
• Remove or cut back the vegetation identified directly next to the structure on both sides.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees near the house so fire cannot climb from ground-level plants up into the tree canopy.
• Keep the area along the curved driveway clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs to maintain access for vehicles.
• Thin scattered shrubs across the property to reduce connected patches of plants that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Maintain wider open gaps between the scattered trees and the structure by removing the closest trees or heavy lower limbs.
• Keep the open terrain areas around the structure free of dead plant material, fallen branches, and dry grass.
• Clear vegetation along the edges of the curved driveway so emergency vehicles can navigate it without obstruction.
